42.entry: McCoy, R. T.; Pavlick, E.; and Linzen, T. 2019. Right for the Wrong Reasons: Diagnosing Syntactic Heuristics in Natural Language Inference. In *Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics*, 3428–3448. DOI 10.18653/v1/P19-1334.
42.safe_claim: Models that learn natural language inference can use a shortcut. The shortcut treats a hypothesis that shares many words with the premise as entailed. The authors build HANS to test this shortcut.

45.entry: Mottin, D.; Marascu, A.; Basu Roy, S.; Das, G.; Palpanas, T.; and Velegrakis, Y. 2013. A Probabilistic Optimization Framework for the Empty-Answer Problem. *Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment* 6(14): 1762–1773. DOI 10.14778/2556549.2556560.
45.safe_claim: When a query returns no answer, a system can suggest new queries that have fewer conditions. The paper gives a framework to choose these relaxations.

46.entry: Shi, J.; Yuan, Z.; Tie, G.; Zhou, P.; Gong, N. Z.; and Sun, L. 2025. Prompt Injection Attack to Tool Selection in LLM Agents. arXiv:2504.19793.
46.safe_claim: An attacker can add a malicious tool document to a tool library. The agent then picks that tool for a task that the attacker chose.

49.entry: Ribeiro, M. T.; Wu, T.; Guestrin, C.; and Singh, S. 2020. Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList. In *Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics*, 4902–4912. DOI 10.18653/v1/2020.acl-main.442.
49.safe_claim: Held-out accuracy can overstate model quality. The authors give CheckList, a method of behavioral tests that comes from software engineering, and a tool that makes many test cases.

51.entry: Feng, Y.; Lu, Z.; Liu, B.; Zhan, L.; and Wu, X.-M. 2023. Towards LLM-driven Dialogue State Tracking. In *Proceedings of the 2023 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing*, 739–755. DOI 10.18653/v1/2023.emnlp-main.48.
51.safe_claim: In the error analysis of the model of Feng et al. on MultiWOZ 2.4, the hotel-type slot has the most errors (338 of 2,835). 78.10 percent of these errors confuse "not mentioned" with "hotel".
